claims.text: Gwanghwamun is the grand main and south gate of Gyeongbokgung Palace, situated in the Jongno District of Seoul.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Originally completed in 1395, it was given its current name in 1426 by King Sejong the Great, with a meaning thought to be 'spreading the dignity and virtue of the country far and wide.'
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The gate has suffered multiple destructions throughout its history, including burning down during the 1592 Imjin War and the Korean War.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: A controversial 1968 reconstruction rebuilt the gate almost entirely out of concrete and steel, symbolizing Korea's modernization at the time.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The most recent large-scale restoration to its original wooden form and placement was opened to the public on August 15, 2010.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In front of the gate stand stone statues of a mythical creature called a 'haetae' (xiezhi), which is traditionally believed to guard against fire and evil spirits.
claims.subject: self
